status: experimental runtime reverted; existing border-fragment fix retained
interpretation: The first integer candidate passes cut geometry and nominal polygon offsets but remains uncertain at all four lattice resolutions. Higher resolution alone does not repair it.

Forty or eighty ordinary refinement steps followed by the existing final paper repair give a valid provisional pair below 2% source-mask error. The 160/320-step alternatives are fail/uncertain. Offset-only refinement retains the initial poorer shape and never resolves lattice uncertainty.

The experimental observer attempts this first-candidate repair before another MILP round. Normal-clock cases improve the motif, but one 1.5x case and both 2x cases run out of repair time. Both 1.5x control cases pass the mask-error target. This provides no robust speed advantage, so the runtime patch was reverted.
The two clock cohorts ran sequentially, experiment then control; this is deadline-pressure evidence, not a hardware-matched causal estimate or a model of the remote runner.

All source-mask features remain final checks. The tiny border fragment is absent even in the useful candidates, so none is a fully accepted reconstruction. Error is agreement with the classified mask, not unavailable original artwork.

visualReview.observations: Short repaired silhouettes retain feet, foliage and narrow neck; timed misses replace these with coarse curved grid blocks. Offset-only runs remain visibly less faithful. Paper failures can be invisible in the woven silhouette.

next: Keep the existing validated border repair. Any future first-candidate recovery must explicitly reserve enough paper-repair time or use a cheaper paper-aware trajectory; do not make uncertainty a pass. Resume material NN work with richer non-lattice supervision and unchanged full-cohort evaluation.
